description: A dense, printable two-column reference for aperture, shutter speed, ISO, examples, mistakes, and terminology.
content: Photography exposure triangle cheatsheet: spoiler-free, print-friendly reference for aperture, shutter speed, ISO, examples, mistakes, glossary, and sources.

metadata.subtitle: A compact, static reference for learning manual exposure.

blocks.title: The exposure triangle
blocks.subtitle: Aperture, shutter speed, and ISO jointly control brightness. Each has a creative side effect.

blocks.title: One exposure, three controls
blocks.alt: Triangular diagram linking aperture, shutter speed, and ISO to exposure.
blocks.caption: Keep brightness constant by compensating a change in one setting with another.

blocks.title: Aperture · f-stop
blocks.content:
**Lower f-number** → wider opening → more light → shallower depth of field.

**Higher f-number** → narrower opening → less light → more depth of field.

Start at f/2 for a portrait or f/8 for a landscape.

blocks.title: Shutter speed · time
blocks.content:
**Faster** (1/1000 s) freezes motion but admits less light.

**Slower** (1/30 s) blurs motion and admits more light.

Handheld starting point: use at least 1/focal-length seconds.

blocks.title: ISO · sensor gain
blocks.content:
**Low ISO** gives cleaner detail but needs more light.

**High ISO** helps in dim light but adds visible noise.

Use the lowest ISO that supports your needed aperture and shutter speed.

blocks.title: Quick settings
blocks.content:
**Portrait:** f/2–f/4, 1/125 s or faster, ISO 100–800.

**Sports:** f/2.8–f/5.6, 1/1000 s, Auto ISO.

**Landscape:** f/8–f/11, tripod if needed, ISO 100.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.content: Do not raise ISO first when the subject is still. First open the aperture or use a slower shutter speed. Do not use a slow handheld shutter speed when camera shake will blur the image.

**Depth of field** — the zone that appears acceptably sharp.

**Stop** — a doubling or halving of light.

**Noise** — random-looking grain or color variation, more visible at high ISO.

**Focal length** — the lens property that changes angle of view and influences handheld shutter-speed needs.
